help.bitDepth.1: Pixel depth is the number of meaningful bits in each sample. It accepts integers from 4 to 32 bits; samples are read as unsigned integers.
help.bitDepth.2: For example, 10-bit values range from 0 to 1023, and 12-bit values from 0 to 4095. In CFA, each array pixel is one sample; in YUV, this applies to individual Y, U and V samples.
help.bitDepth.3: Pixel depth must not exceed container size. A 10-bit sample can use a 10-bit or 16-bit container; the latter has 6 padding bits that do not contribute to the sample value.
help.containerBits.1: Container size is the number of bits occupied by each stored sample. It accepts integers from 4 to 32 and must be at least the pixel depth.
help.containerBits.2: For example, 10-bit samples in 10-bit containers are packed consecutively; in 16-bit containers they occupy 2 bytes each. Non-byte containers are bit-packed, with each row starting on a byte boundary and unused end-of-row bits treated as padding.
help.containerBits.3: When the container exceeds the pixel depth, alignment selects the low or high bits. Container size also determines minimum row bytes, frame size and sequence frame offsets.
help.containerBits.4: Auto uses the pixel depth for bit-packed files (for example, 12bit-packed uses 12 bits); otherwise it rounds up to the smallest whole-byte container. Changing the container selection preserves this packing hint. An explicit container size always takes precedence; Auto does not detect packing from image content or file length.
help.offset.1: Unit: bytes. Skip this many bytes from the start of the file before reading; 0 starts at the beginning. Must be a non-negative integer.
help.offset.2: For example, if the file has a 16-byte header, set the offset to 16 to read the image after the header.
help.offset.3: Frame size is calculated from the current dimensions, format, bit depth and row pitches. If there is not enough data for a frame, an error appears by the dimensions; if the offset exceeds the file size, an error appears by the offset.
help.offset.4: For sequences, this is the start of frame 1: frame N starts at offset + (N − 1) × bytes per frame. Only complete frames are shown; an incomplete tail is ignored. Changing the offset pauses playback and returns to frame 1.
help.matrix.1: Determines how YUV (Y′CbCr) luma and chroma are converted to RGB. An incorrect matrix can shift hue or saturation.
help.matrix.2: BT.601 is commonly used for SD video; BT.709 for HD; BT.2020 for UHD video encoded to that standard. This viewer uses the non-constant-luminance BT.2020 conversion.
help.matrix.3: Use the matrix declared by the source or encoder, rather than relying on resolution. Formats such as NV12, I420 and P010 describe sampling and storage, but do not determine the color matrix.
help.matrix.4: The matrix affects color and chroma previews, but not luma-only grayscale. This option does not decode HDR (PQ / HLG) or convert to the display color gamut.
help.range.1: Determines how sample values map to black, white and chroma intensity. Match the quantization range of the source. This setting is independent of the color matrix.
help.range.2: Limited · Video range: at 8 bits, nominal Y black and white are 16–235. U / V nominally span 16–240, with neutral chroma at 128.
help.range.3: Full · Full range: at 8 bits, Y black and white are 0–255. U / V use 0–255, with neutral chroma at 128. At n bits, the full range is 0–(2ⁿ−1) and neutral chroma is 2ⁿ⁻¹.
help.range.4: For higher-bit-depth Limited data, scale the values by 2⁽ⁿ⁻⁸⁾. For example, at 10 bits: Y is 64–940, U / V are 64–960, and neutral chroma is 512. These are sample values before shifting within the storage container.
help.range.5: Reading Limited data as Full typically produces gray blacks and reduced contrast. Reading Full data as Limited may clip shadows and highlights. Prefer the source documentation.

help.alignment.1: Needed only when the container exceeds the pixel depth. Padding placement determines where meaningful bits sit within a container; byte order is configured separately.
help.alignment.2: Zero-fill high bits: meaningful bits occupy the low bits, so the value is stored directly. For an 8-bit pixel in a 10-bit container, 255 is stored as 00 11111111.
help.alignment.3: Zero-fill low bits: shift the value left by container size minus pixel depth. For an 8-bit pixel in a 10-bit container, 255 << 2 is stored as 11111111 00 (1020) and read back as 255. This setting interprets existing data without modifying the file.
hint.alphaPercent: 0% = RGB only (IR fully transparent); 100% = IR only (IR fully opaque).

demosaic.schema.title: Bayer demosaic coefficients
demosaic.schema.variationPenalty: Suppress sharpening of smooth color variation.
demosaic.schema.directions: Clockwise image coordinates: 0° right, 90° down. Opposite rays are independent.
demosaic.schema.strength: Normalized gradient threshold; start at 0 and increase strictly.
demosaic.schema.uniform: Uniform-weight fraction: 1 = balanced, 0 = fully edge weighted.
demosaic.schema.edgePower: Larger values reject samples across color edges more strongly.
demosaic.schema.tangentBias: Preference for candidates along the edge tangent.
